deep.reconstruction:
This page is the third sheet of an axiomatic draft. The surrounding pages in the folder are unrelated administrative pay tables. The page reuses the same template as the previous sheet: one H-construction per 'Hot n' axiom. H assigns to every small category A a category H(A), meant to be a homotopy category of H-valued presheaves (or diagrams) over A.

Axiom (Hot 2): for every functor f: A -> B in Cat, the restriction functor f^*_H: H(B) -> H(A) has a LEFT adjoint f_!^H, which should go H(A) -> H(B). Grothendieck first wrote f^*: Hot(A), crossed it out, and replaced it with the H-version.

He then adds a caution: perhaps one should restrict the axiom to 'cofibrantes' f. The most natural reading is cofibred functors (opfibrations, in the sense of SGA 1), for which f_! should be computable fibrewise.

Special case B = Delta_0 (the final category, a point). Here f is the projection pi_A: A -> Delta_0 and f_! becomes a functor H(A) -> Hot_H. He denotes it ∫_A and calls it the 'foncteur d'intégration', playing the role of a colimit over A. In modern terms this is the homotopy colimit / left homotopy Kan extension to the point.

Transitivity: composing f with pi_B gives pi_A = pi_B o f. Since left adjoints compose, ∫_A X = ∫_B f_!(X). This is Fubini for homotopy colimits.

Marginal NB, partly illegible: the existence of the f_! follows from the existence of the integrals ∫ (on the H(A)'s), together with colimits / pointwise considerations in H(B). This is presumably the pointwise Kan formula: (f_!X)_b = ∫_{A/b} X|_{A/b}.

Axiom (Hot 3): dually, there are cointegration operations ∏_A (homotopy limits), and more generally right adjoints f_*^H to the f^*_H.

In sum, this is an early (1983) formulation of the core existence axiom of a derivator. The adjoints f_! and f_* along all functors of small categories correspond to Der3 in later terminology. The page also notes the Fubini/transitivity and the pointwise reconstruction of f_! from integrals over comma categories.
errors: The image clearly writes f_!^H : H(B) -> H(A); the left adjoint of f^*: H(B) -> H(A) must go H(A) -> H(B). This is a slip in the manuscript; the text immediately afterwards (∫_A: H(A) -> Hot_H) uses the correct direction.

The NB claim that f_! exists given the integrals ∫ is only correct if the Kan-formula values (f_!X)_b = ∫_{A/b} X glue to an object of H(B). In a homotopy category of diagrams this does not follow from objectwise data alone. It needs either an underlying model or a derivator-style axiom (Der2/Der4) controlling the base change of f_! to comma categories. This gap is exactly what later derivator theory isolates.

The hesitation about restricting to 'cofibrant' f is unnecessary in the final theory: derivators require f_! for all functors. Restricting to opfibrations would, however, be enough to recover the general case via comma-category factorisation, so the worry is harmless rather than wrong.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean early (1983) statement of the derivator axioms with the 'integration' notation. It is historically nice as a dated precursor of Les Dérivateurs, written in parallel with Pursuing Stacks. Mathematically, though, everything here is well documented in Grothendieck's own later texts and in Heller/Franke/Cisinski. The 'cofibrant f' hesitation is a minor variant with no new content.
transcription_corrections: The line rendered as 'H(A) désignant ici [?] convenablement [?] en du rapport [?] pour A' is largely illegible. Only 'H(A) désignant ici ... convenablement ... A' is reasonably secure; it likely refers to the H-category attached to A.
'Il faudrait faire attention' is more plausibly 'Il faut faire attention s'il ne faudrait pas'. 'cofibrantes' is underlined, and the marginal insertion before 'se borner' looks like 'mais' or 'ou'.
In the manuscript the word 'gauche' in 'a un adjoint à gauche' is underlined.
The f_! line indeed reads 'H(B) -> H(A)' in the image, an author's slip for H(A) -> H(B).
The marginal NB is written diagonally and is only partly legible: 'NB L'existence des f_! découle de l'existence des ∫ (des H(A)), ... dans H(B)...'.
(Hot 3) is marked with a circled '3' followed by 'Opérations ∏_A de co-intégration, ... des f_*^H adjoints à droite des f^*_H'.
